meta.title: 15 MISTAKES Tourists Keep Making when Traveling to Vietnam in 2026!
meta.description:
Planning a trip to Vietnam in 2026? Watch this before you go. Vietnam travel tips can save you money, stress, scams, and a lot of rookie mistakes before your trip even starts. In this video, we cover 15 mistakes tourists keep making in Vietnam, from flights, visas, and money exchange to hotels, taxis, Airbnb, safety, and communication with locals.

After living in Vietnam for 13 years, Attorney Ken Duong shares the things he genuinely wishes he knew before visiting. Some mistakes are small but expensive. Others can ruin your trip before you even land. If you are planning to visit Vietnam in 2026, this is the kind of practical advice most travel videos leave out.

We also cover Vietnam travel tips for first-time visitors, including the best way to handle ATMs, ride-hailing apps, domestic transportation, where tourists overspend, what to know about short-term rentals, and why some famous recommendations are not always the best ones. There are also a few bucket-list suggestions that go beyond the lazy internet checklist.

If you are planning to move to Vietnam, this video might save you time, money, and a lot of unnecessary stress.

Don’t make these mistakes, learn them before you land.

Domestic flight tips: if you are bringing a checked bag, try to prepay for your checked luggage. If you’re unable to pay for your checked luggage for your flight back, go and pay for your checked luggage when you land. I had to pay full price, which was more than the flight itself. Vietnam airlines said you save 50% off when paying 6 hours in advance, but won’t let you check in for your flight until 90 mins before your flight. 

Bring a portable fan, it is super hot when waiting in that long customs line after landing in Vietnam.

I like riding my motorbikes  here although the traffic is daunting for the first time visitor i find it relative easy even in the city somehow what looks like traffic chaos just works. Having said that its  getting worse every year,  lot of cars on the roads compared to 5 or 10 years ago. Tourists visiting Vietnam will totally enjoy the experience, just relax stay inside the law, bring a good attitude with you.   Unfortunately in some cases it is some  tourists who disregard and ignore  the privilege of being in this wonderful country  can spoil it but its rare and usually delt with quickly,  VN police do not play around.

comments.author: @PervyK
comments.text:
Brining usd seriously take it serioulsy when it comes to exchanging pristine new 100 bills. The smallest crease, blemish, and writing will seriously ding down its worth. a bengamin with a small defect will tank to 70-50% worth in exchange. A single fold makes it near worthless. It needs to be the most perfect bills you can find for good exchange.

For traveling to local places in the city - avoid the tourist traps where tourguides drop folks at. If you see alot of foreginers in a spot you are in the wrong spot to get any decent food for the local price. Travel down the street and you'll end up finding things 20-50% the price at higher quality and quantity sometimes because it snot stuff people know they can upsell for highest profit margins to foreigners who don't know what a good Pho or snack should taste like. 

Keep viet cash on you for when you gotta buy your way out of something. Bribing is just a thing over there. Don't give to much, dont cop a attitude or start a big commotion. You'll always lose. Obey the laws bc it'll be your hinny if they call you on it. 

Vietnam is extraordinarily safe. But petty theft like phone/wallet/bag snatching is still a thing as is any country. Just keep mind to have a iron grip. It really is a safe country though as long as you're not the one causing the problems.

Oh and dont drink the tap water, and only bottled/filtered. Eat nothing raw and cook that stuff good. The first few things you eat will dictate the rest fo your trip. Don't eat weird stuff and find yourself having diarrhea both ends. Acclimate a bit haha. Take it easy the first day or so.  Folks over there take pills for parasites occasionally for a reason. You may not be built for that off the boat.
